label: Kimi K3.1 Pro
output:
Straight answer, Rohan. You and Divya trusted me with real money, so you both deserve more than “it’s complicated” over dinner.

Yes, I let go of six of our fourteen people last Friday. It was the worst day I’ve had at FixKaro—worse than failing maths in second sem, and that involved an actual lecture at home. Everyone got two months’ pay, and I’ve already helped four of them get interviews. That doesn’t make the situation good, but I tried not to make a bad day worse for them.

The immediate trigger was the Hyderabad bridge round falling through on 28 Oct. The term sheet was basically ready. On the call, the partner said “we love the energy,” and then went quiet for 11 days. Apparently the energy was not sufficient to power a bank transfer. I should have planned better for the round not closing; that part is on me.

After the cuts, we have roughly five months of runway. That is breathing room, not a safety certificate.

On your ₹3 lakh specifically: you and Divya invested in the 2025 friends round, on the same terms as everyone else. **The money is at risk, but it is not gone.** FixKaro is still operating. I cannot promise that your capital is safe or that you’ll get it back, because I genuinely don’t know how this ends. If we can’t make the business work, losing the investment is a real possibility. Anyone giving you a cleaner guarantee right now would be lying.

Where the business actually stands: we have around 41k monthly users. The plumbers and electricians side is growing. AC servicing is bleeding money, so we’re shutting that down instead of continuing to feed the machine because it looks impressive on a slide.

Our focus now is housing-society tie-ups. Three societies in HSR have already signed pilots. They’re pilots, not proof that we’ve won—but they give us a real place to prove the model. My honest view is that we have a genuine shot. It is not a sure thing, and I’m not going to do the “we’re crushing it” routine while secretly crushing Maggi at midnight.

Speaking of which, I’m fine. Tired, but fine. I’ve eaten so much 11pm office Maggi that the security uncle now asks whether I want masala or plain, which is either touching concern or the beginning of a menu. Amma also asked me last week if TCS is still hiring, so investor confidence at home is currently “cautious.”

Rohan, let’s not try to settle your and Divya’s questions in between dosa plans. I’ll call you both properly this week and show you the actual numbers—cash, burn, runway, the society pilots and what happens in each scenario. No deck gymnastics, no LinkedIn adjectives. Ask me whatever you want, including the uncomfortable stuff. You’ve earned that right.

And yes, Ajay, I know six isn’t half of fourteen. At least one of us has improved at maths since college.

I’m coming Saturday. Pranav is buying, which is currently my most reliable funding commitment. 🍻
